verdict.rationale: Babylon.js ships an Inspector described as offering "visual debugging and scene editing" and runtime scene analysis, plus a visual Node Material Editor for shaders. Artists can also compose scenes in 3ds Max, Maya or Blender and export them. Nothing shows a dedicated editor with viewport, inspector and prefabs being the primary way to build levels; the core workflow is code-first, via the Playground and the npm/TypeScript APIs. Missing for 10: a full standalone scene/level editor, prefab or reusable scene-composition support, evidence that visual editing is the primary authoring workflow, and independent hands-on corroboration of the Inspector's editing depth.
